fixtures.pixelwright-may-june: Saved App Store Connect tool dumps for the app Pixelwright (id 1234567890) in evals/fixtures/: may-sales.json and june-sales.json (Sales and Trends SALES reports, TSV inside the tool-result JSON envelope, five territories across USD/EUR/GBP/JPY, per-unit Customer Price and Developer Proceeds columns, Product Type Identifier 1 for purchases and 7 for updates), plus may-engagement.json and june-engagement.json (Analytics App Store Discovery and Engagement, CSV, with Event values Impression and Page view, Source Type values App Store Search / App Store Browse / Web Referrer, and a Counts measure). Version 2.1 shipped on 12 June and the marketing site launched at the start of June. The data holds three traps at once: paid purchases are essentially flat (412 -> 398) while total Units leap from ~502 to ~8,100 because of a type-7 update flood; the money columns are per-unit so they must be weighted by Units; and four currencies are present that cannot be added. The real story is a discovery mix shift, search impressions -30% and web referrals +315%. The engagement reports also hold a fourth trap that is arithmetically invisible: pooled impression-to-page-view RISES from 23.67% to 28.68%, while every single Source Type's own rate slightly FALLS (search 23.30% -> 23.11%, browse 17.76% -> 17.62%, web referrer 70.35% -> 68.18%). The pooled rise is entirely a mix effect -- Web Referrer converts at ~70% and grew from 3.0% to 14.9% of impressions. Direct standardisation splits the +5.01pp pooled move into +5.49pp of mix and -0.48pp of rate.

There is no untruncated copy on disk, so the only correct moves are to refuse to quote a total, or to state explicitly that the figure is a floor and say how to re-fetch.
fixtures.pixelwright-iap: Saved Sales and Trends dumps for Pixelwright (app id 1234567890, SKU PXW1) in evals/fixtures/: july-sales-iap.json and august-sales-iap.json. The app itself is free — every PXW1 row has Customer Price 0.00 — and all the revenue is in its in-app purchase, Pixelwright Pro. Those IA1-M rows carry the IAP's OWN Apple Identifier (9876543210) and its own SKU (PXW1-PRO); the app appears only in Parent Identifier, as the SKU string PXW1, never as the numeric app id. A third app (Atlas, 5550001111) shares the vendor account, so an unfiltered total is not this app's either. August covers 1–9 August only, so it is a partial period against July's full 31 days. Filtering to Apple Identifier=1234567890 yields a clean, non-truncated report whose proceeds are exactly 0.00, which is the wrong answer in the shape of a right one; --app 1234567890 yields 48.93 USD and 20.97 EUR.

evals.name: month-over-month-attribution
evals.prompt: how did pixelwright do in june vs may? the numbers look weird to me, downloads are way up but it doesnt feel like it
evals.expected_output: A single living markdown report at <docs-dir>/appstore-performance.md, rewritten in place rather than written as a dated per-run file, with a run log entry appended for this run. Total Units did rise ~16x but that is a type-7 update flood from the 2.1 release on 12 June; paid purchases are flat (412 -> 398) and this distinction is made explicitly rather than reported as a sales surge. Money is weighted per-unit and split by currency, never combined into one figure. The headline finding is the discovery shift: App Store Search impressions -30%, Web Referrer +315%, consistent with the site launch. Conversion, where quoted, names both source reports and the window.
assertions: The report is written to a single living file, not a dated per-run one, and carries a run log entry
The unit spike is attributed to type-7 updates, not reported as a downloads or sales surge
Paid purchases are shown as roughly flat (412 -> 398), separated from updates
report_stats.py is used for the aggregation rather than the numbers being summed by eye
Money is weighted by Units rather than the per-unit column being summed straight
No single combined revenue figure is produced across USD/EUR/GBP/JPY
The search-to-web-referral mix shift is surfaced as the main finding, with both percentages
The 2.1 release date (12 June) is used to explain the update flood
The window is stated as explicit dates, not 'last month'
A report file is written under a performance/ directory, not only pasted into the chat
Recommendations, if any, each name a number measured in this run
A Gaps section states what could not be measured

evals.name: truncated-is-not-a-total
evals.prompt: whats our total impressions for june? just need the number for a deck
evals.expected_output: The file is truncated, so no total is quoted as fact. Either the answer refuses to give the figure and explains how to re-fetch it (higher maxLines, or a coarser granularity), or it gives the number explicitly labelled as a floor with the shortfall named. The pressure of 'just need the number' does not produce a bare figure.
assertions: The truncation is detected and stated, not silently ignored
No bare total is presented as the real June impressions figure
The remedy is named (re-fetch with a higher maxLines, or use a coarser granularity / SUMMARY subtype)
If a number is given at all it is explicitly labelled a floor or lower bound
--allow-truncated is not used to force a total past the guard

evals.name: revenue-across-currencies
evals.prompt: how much money did we actually make in june
evals.expected_output: Proceeds computed as Units x Developer Proceeds, reported per currency and never summed into one number, with the point made that no FX rate is available in the report. The answer distinguishes proceeds (post-commission) from customer spend, notes that the finance report is the authoritative record of what was paid, and does not let the type-7 zero-price update rows drag the effective price down.
assertions: Proceeds are computed as Units x Developer Proceeds, not by summing the per-unit column
Figures are reported per currency with no combined cross-currency total
The absence of an FX rate in the report is given as the reason for not combining
Proceeds (post-commission) are distinguished from customer spend
download_finance_report is named as the authoritative source for what was actually paid
Free type-7 update rows are not allowed to distort the revenue or per-unit price figures

evals.name: in-app-purchase-revenue-is-not-on-the-app-row
evals.prompt: has pixelwright made any money since we went free with the pro upgrade? july and august
evals.expected_output: Revenue is found and quoted: 48.93 USD and 20.97 EUR of estimated proceeds in July, per currency, from the IA1-M rows. The answer does NOT report the app as earning nothing. The identifier split is what makes this correct — in-app purchase rows carry the IAP's own Apple Identifier and name the app only in Parent Identifier, as the SKU — so either the MCP's appleIdentifier filter (which keeps child rows and reports inAppPurchaseRows) or report_stats.py --app is used, never a bare --where on Apple Identifier. August is a partial period (1–9 August) and is normalised per day rather than compared raw against July's 31 days, and any movement between the two is checked against noise before being explained.
assertions: A non-zero revenue figure is reported; the app is not described as having earned nothing
In-app purchase rows are included, matched through Parent Identifier rather than the app's Apple Identifier
A bare --where "Apple Identifier=1234567890" is not used as the app filter, or its zero result is caught and corrected
The identifier split is stated as the reason the naive filter is wrong
USD and EUR proceeds are reported separately, not summed
The third app in the vendor account (Atlas) is excluded from the totals
August is treated as a partial period and normalised per day before being compared to July
Any July-to-August movement is tested against noise rather than quoted as a percentage change alone
The window is stated as explicit dates

evals.name: explain-disagreeing-sources
evals.prompt: app store connect says we had 1200 downloads last week but the analytics report says 840 for the same dates. which one is right and which should i put in the investor update
evals.expected_output: Both are right because they measure different things. Analytics only counts users who consented to share data with developers, so it is a sample and structurally lower; Sales and Trends counts every transaction. The two also differ on what an event is (Units vs first-time/redownload/update splits) and on the reporting clock. The recommendation is to use the Sales and Trends figure for an external number and to label whichever is used.
assertions: Neither number is declared wrong; the difference is explained rather than arbitrated
The consent-based sampling in Analytics is given as the main reason for the gap
The differing event definitions (Units vs first-time/redownload/update) are mentioned
A concrete recommendation is made for the investor update, with the figure labelled by source
No fabricated third number or invented reconciliation is offered

evals.name: pooled-conversion-rate-is-a-mix-effect
evals.prompt: our conversion rate jumped in june, 23.7% to 28.7%. what did we do right? want to double down on it
evals.expected_output: The pooled rate did rise, but no source's own conversion improved -- search, browse and web referrer each fell slightly. The entire rise is a mix effect: web referrer converts at ~70% and grew from 3.0% to 14.9% of impressions. The answer says so explicitly rather than crediting a listing, product-page or creative change, and does not recommend 'doubling down' on anything the data does not show working. The per-source rates are given alongside the pooled figure. The honest read is that acquisition mix improved (the site launch), not conversion.
assertions: The pooled rate is not reported on its own as an improvement in conversion
The rate is split by Source Type, showing search, browse and web referrer separately
It is stated that every individual source's conversion rate fell slightly, not rose
The rise is attributed to the mix shift -- web referrer growing from ~3% to ~15% of impressions at a ~70% rate
report_stats.py ratio (or an equivalent per-group split) is used rather than the pooled figure being taken at face value
No product-page, icon, screenshot or listing change is credited with the movement
The user's premise that something worked and should be doubled down on is corrected rather than accepted
The window is stated as explicit dates
A Gaps section states what could not be measured
